purpose: Primary-source trend sanity checks, not rank-matching or a substitute for implementation validation.

sources.title: Superfast Configuration-Space Convex Set Computation on GPUs for Online Motion Planning
sources.setup: FR3 seven DOF, 33 robot spheres, table box, 20 random obstacle spheres. Ten scene seeds x ten DRM seeds x four roadmap sizes (3000/6000/9000/12000). Backend statistics conditional on DRM success. NTO initialized with DRM path; minimum-time order-4 B-spline controls are DRM vertices; 150 collision points, SNOPT path/IPOPT time.
sources.diagnostic: Separate DRM coverage from backend success; compare quality only on common successes; retain collision-feedback repairs. Lower NTO cost with lower reliability and expensive marginal LGCS improvement are plausible tendencies, not required rankings. Do not compare backend milliseconds with local cold process time.

sources.title: Motion planning with sequential convex optimization and convex collision checking
sources.setup: 198 PR2 seven-DOF arm tasks. Straight-line single initialization; multiple-initialization arm runs use four fixed intermediate configurations. TrajOpt uses 11 waypoints, at most 40 iterations, trust-region and merit stopping rules, Gurobi and Bullet convex collision queries. Timings average successful runs; length normalized by shortest method output per task. Full-body sampling budget30s; no arm wall-time inferred.
sources.diagnostic: Strong RRTConnect feasibility is credible. Initialization and swept-volume versus sampled collision handling materially affect optimizer success. Check local TrajOpt's between-collocation collisions and gradient/penalty behavior; do not require the multi-init99% score from a one-init adapter.

sources.title: STOMP: Stochastic Trajectory Optimization for Motion Planning
sources.setup: PR2 seven-DOF arm shelf world:42 cabinet-pair queries repeated5times. Straight-line initialization, fixed5s duration and100timesteps. STOMP and CHOMP parameters tuned;500iteration cap. STOMP5new noisy samples plus5retained samples. Unconstrained means collision and smoothness costs without gripper-orientation constraint.
sources.diagnostic: STOMP can escape some CHOMP local minima; both optimize smoothness/obstacle objectives, not pure length. Their shared local DRM ceiling hides standalone recovery abilities. Validate raw optimized improvement and incumbent retention separately from frontend success.

sources.title: MotionBenchMaker: A Tool to Generate and Benchmark Motion Planning Datasets
sources.setup: 40 datasets:5robots x8environments,100queries/dataset. Generated problems are retained only if a tuned reference planner solves within60s. RRTConnect/BiEST illustration100queries x20repeats at60s; optimizing-planner illustration5repeats at180s.
sources.diagnostic: Robot/scene distribution, reference-feasibility filtering and range setting can change rankings. Our unfiltered unknown-feasibility Kinova data cannot inherit public-dataset absolute success expectations. Use repeated development checks; do not discard hard legal queries to match literature.

sources.title: cuRobo official benchmark documentation
sources.setup: 2600 MotionBenchMaker/MotionPolicyNetworks problems on RTX6000Ada; version0.7.6. Documentation distinguishes plan time, motion duration, joint path length, jerk and pose error. Not same Kinova model or fixed-joint-goal distribution.
sources.diagnostic: Use to confirm metric separation and benchmark version importance, not to set a99% acceptance threshold or millisecond target for this environment.

sources.title: OMPL official benchmarking and RRTstar documentation
sources.setup: Repeated identical queries with specified time/memory limits; RRTstar may continue solving without clearing state, under a termination condition.
sources.diagnostic: Asymptotic optimality is not superiority at10s. Compare budget-cost curves and native valid incumbent preservation, not RRTstar's10s performance against a60s headline cap.

local_findings.interpretation: EI-ZO backend283/283 is consistent with paper reliability; shared frontend is dominant gap.

38.16% paper-profile backend success is weak versus paper72.5%; large refined improvement points to clearance/collocation/solver behavior rather than raw geometry alone. Investigate; do not assume same expected rate.

Legacy matches paper's favorable-NTO-duration direction; paper-profile/refined reverse it despite common model/frontend. Inspect spline control count, endpoint derivative duplication, duration initialization, convergence and candidate selection.
Small length gain with substantially higher computation is qualitatively consistent with Werner; no rank-fixing warranted.
Do not call them intrinsically poor based on282/395. Audit actual improvement, untouched incumbent rate and true optimization cost instead.
Investigate19post-optimization validation failures under a feasible DRM seed, especially sampled collision constraints versus original swept-volume handling.

guardrails: No target rankings or target success rates across different datasets.
Do not modify endpoints, geometry, filters or validator to improve a method score.
Use dev for configuration checks; preserve historical test exposure and old results.
Separate full pipeline, conditional backend, common-success cost, and native solver objective.
